Ian Talbert

I am a mechanical engineer focused on the intersection of aggressive kinematic design, high-strain dynamic impacts, and pragmatic manufacturing. Whether engineering an autonomous planetary sample acquisition system with JPL-inspired microspines or designing three-pound battlebots that accelerate 800-Joule steel bars to fifteen thousand revolutions per minute, I believe true mechanical engineering is proven where theory collides violently with reality.

Currently completing my Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering at Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology, I serve as President of the Rose-Hulman Combat Robotics Team. Over the past three seasons, I have designed nine scratch-built combat robots, secured back-to-back Midwest Robot Combat Association (MRCA) championships across the 1lb and 3lb divisions, and earned 29 podium placements and 13 tournament victories in 60 career bouts.

My engineering practice is grounded in hands-on metal fabrication—manual and CNC milling, lathe operations, precision sheet-metal forming, and extensive 3D printing across FDM, SLS nylon, and composite resins. In industry, I have developed high-rate automated assembly tooling at Broan-NuTone, designed dynamic drone propulsion test stands at VEX Robotics, and deployed autonomous mobile transport robotics at GE Appliances.
